title: Non-Abelian Anyon Condensation: a Path-Integral Monte Carlo Approach
authors: Rafael Flores-Calderón, Frank Pollmann, Michael Knap
abstract: Transitions out of non-Abelian topological order are difficult to describe in microscopic quantum models with numerical methods that remain tractable at large scales. We develop a sign-free path-integral framework for Kitaev quantum doubles $\mathcal D(G)$ by organizing single-link perturbations in terms of non-invertible electric and magnetic 1-form symmetries that proliferate distinct anyon species. For any finite group $G$, an exact $\textit{matterization}$ isometry introduces vertex degrees of freedom and maps the link-only model onto a $G$ gauge--Higgs theory. Furthermore, the 1-form symmetries of the fixed point allow us to define generalized Fredenhagen--Marcu order parameters that become finite when the corresponding anyons condense. For $G = S_3$, quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that proliferating a non-Abelian electric anyon drives a first-order transition in which all nontrivial electric anyons condense. In the purely magnetic limit, the model reduces to a $(2+1)$D pure $G$ gauge theory; for $G=S_3$, it exhibits a first-order confinement transition, diagnosed by the onset of a Wilson-loop area law and the restoration of an emergent magnetic 1-form symmetry. These results provide a unified numerical framework for non-Abelian anyon condensation, confinement, and generalized symmetry breaking.
summary: This work develops a novel, sign-free path-integral Monte Carlo approach to study transitions out of non-Abelian topological order in Kitaev quantum double models. By mapping the system to a gauge-Higgs theory, the authors successfully diagnose non-Abelian anyon condensation and confinement transitions. The results provide a unified numerical tool for understanding complex topological phase transitions in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty of describing transitions out of non-Abelian topological order using standard numerical methods at large scales.
main_result: The authors provide a unified numerical framework demonstrating non-Abelian anyon condensation and confinement transitions in Kitaev quantum doubles for $G=S_3$. Specifically, electric anyon proliferation drives a first-order condensation transition.
method: The methodology involves developing a sign-free path-integral framework by mapping the link-only model onto a $G$ gauge–Higgs theory via an exact matterization isometry. Quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to analyze the resulting lattice gauge-Higgs model.
model_or_system: The system is based on Kitaev quantum doubles $\mathcal D(G)$ defined on a lattice, which are perturbed by single-link operators to probe anyon condensation. This model is mathematically transformed into a $(2+1)$D $G$ gauge–Higgs theory.
key_observables: Generalized Fredenhagen–Marcu (FM) order parameters (for condensation) and Wilson loops (for confinement).
important_parameters: The group $G$ (specifically $S_3$), and coupling ratios like $\lambda_a/\kappa$ controlling the type of anyon proliferation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a unitary transformation and an isometry to map the quantum double model to a classical gauge-Higgs theory, and the use of the Trotter approximation in the path integral.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the path integral lifting to a gauge-Higgs theory, the action of local operators via the matterization circuit, and the diagnostic plots showing the onset of the Wilson-loop area law and the finite jump in FM order parameters.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the physical problem and the need for a tractable numerical framework. It then details the mathematical machinery: the matterization isometry and the transformation of the Hamiltonian to the gauge-Higgs form. Finally, it applies this framework to analyze specific transitions (condensation and confinement) using Monte Carlo simulations and order parameters.
why_interesting: The rigorous development of a sign-free path-integral method to study topological phase transitions in lattice gauge theories is highly relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated quantum matter systems.
